$schema: Dev notes — deviations, discoveries, decisions, blockers, resolutions captured during build

notes.content: Vite content-negotiates CSS files at /src/**/*.css: requests with Accept: text/css (what <link rel=stylesheet> sends) get raw CSS, while JS-module requests get an HMR-wrapped JS shim. The css-effect renderer's ensureStylesheet() <link> approach therefore works correctly in dev without any extra config. This negotiation should also apply to /assets/effects/*.css after CP2's relocation since assets/ also lives under the project root.

Verification limitation: the checkpoint's testing_strategy is a manual visual browser test (bg video looping + CRT overlay). I verified all the underlying plumbing — npm install clean, dev server boots cleanly in ~400ms with no errors, all routes return 200 with correct content-types (HTML, JSON, video/mp4, text/css, JS modules), and `vite build` succeeds producing valid dist output. The actual rendered pixels were not visually confirmed because no browser is available in this environment. User should run `npm --prefix apps/scene-engine run dev` and open the shown URL to confirm the visual.

scene-renderer.js previously set `el.style.inset = '0'` unconditionally so layers fill the stage. With glyph-group's positional layout (left/top/transform from applyPosition), inset:0 would override left/top. Adjusted scene-renderer to only set inset:'0' when layer.position is absent. Position-bearing layers retain the offsets set by their renderer; full-stage layers (media, effect) keep inset:0 as before.

CODECAINE.css-layers.svg from font-creation outputs is ~1.7 MB (not the ~32 KB the plan estimated). The SVG is one big mass of cubic-Bezier <path d=...> data per layer; this affects fetch latency on first scene load but is fine for a hardcoded title scene. Future optimization: could compress with SVGO, or pre-flatten to a binary asset, but that's a CP6+ concern, not CP2's job.

Verification limitation (same as CP1): no browser available in this environment so the visual outcome (bg video + chrome CODECAINE centered top-third + CRT overlay) is not eyeballed. Verified all plumbing: `vite build` produces valid dist; dev server returns 200 with correct content-types for /assets/registry.json (application/json), /scenes/title/scene.json (application/json), /assets/media/test-fire-2.mp4 (video/mp4, 16.2 MB), /assets/effects/crt-overlay.css (text/css), /assets/glyphs/CODECAINE.css-layers.svg (image/svg+xml, 1.78 MB). User should run `npm --prefix apps/scene-engine run dev` to confirm the visual.

Repo .gitignore had a blanket `assets/` rule (with an existing exception for the font-creation pipeline inputs) that would have silently dropped the new apps/scene-engine/assets/ tree from version control. Added matching `!apps/scene-engine/assets/` and `!apps/scene-engine/assets/**` exceptions so registry.json, the media/ and effects/ trees, and the CODECAINE SVG track properly. Pre-existing .css-files and .mp4 went through via `git mv` because they were already tracked.

Combined CP3 task 3.1.1 (named-only loop) and 3.1.2 (full dual-branch loop with foreign children) into a single edit since task 3.1.2's actions REFACTOR what 3.1.1 just installed (e.g. applySubLayerOverride signature change from svgRoot→el, viewBox extracted into parseViewBox helper). Writing the intermediate state would have been overwritten 30 seconds later. Final glyph-group.js matches the post-3.1.2 spec exactly.

Vite emits an INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT warning at build time because asset-renderers/index.js is statically imported elsewhere AND dynamically imported by glyph-group.js. The warning is benign (the dynamic import just resolves to the same chunk; cycle works correctly at runtime). Plan task 3.1.2 anticipated this. Vite build still succeeds; production bundle is correct.

Verification limitation (same as CP1, CP2): no browser available so the visual outcome (fire visibly bleeding through CODECAINE letterforms with chrome on top, hue-shifted red fill, missing chrome-environment-reflection pass) is not eyeballed. Verified all plumbing: vite build succeeds (only the expected dynamic-import warning); dev server boots in ~85 ms with no errors; all routes return 200 with correct content-types — /scenes/title/scene.json (application/json, 1139 B with new children array), /assets/registry.json (application/json, 379 B with in-text-fire entry), /assets/media/test-fire-3.mp4 (video/mp4, 14.07 MB), /assets/glyphs/CODECAINE.css-layers.svg (image/svg+xml, 1.78 MB). User should run `npm --prefix apps/scene-engine run dev` to confirm the visual.

Hierarchy row label spec said `${layer.id} [${layer.type}]`, but named-sub-layer children only carry { id, layer, properties? } — no type. That would render rows like `extrusion-shadow [undefined]`. Added `?? 'sub-layer'` fallback so the five CODECAINE sub-rows label as `[sub-layer]` (named-layer overrides) or their actual type for foreign-asset children (e.g. `in-text-fire [media]`). Top-level layers always have type so they render unchanged.

Build only emits the runtime entry (single dist/index.html). The editor is dev-only this checkpoint — multi-page Vite build (rollupOptions.input mapping editor + scene-per-page entries) is CP6's explicit concern. Confirmed dev mode: GET /editor/ returns the editor HTML, GET /editor/src/main.js returns Vite-transformed module, GET /scenes/title/scene.json + /assets/registry.json both 200. No vite.config.js change required for CP4.

Verification limitation (same as CP1–CP3): no browser available so the visual outcome (4-panel layout, scene rendered in canvas, hierarchy tree with chevron toggle, inspector populated on click, asset browser grouped by type) is not eyeballed. Verified all plumbing: vite build succeeds; dev server boots in ~80 ms; /editor/ + /editor/src/main.js + /scenes/title/scene.json all 200. Expected interactive behaviour: click codecaine-logo chevron → 5 sub-rows collapse/expand; click a row → inspector renders read-only properties + (for resolvable layers) yellow outline appears on canvas. User should run `npm --prefix apps/scene-engine run dev` and open /editor/?scene=title to confirm.

Inspector subscribes to scene-changed for live re-render so canvas reflects edits, but every keystroke on a debounced number input triggers a scene-changed event — a naive replaceChildren would steal focus mid-edit. Added an early-return guard  in renderInspector. When user is actively editing, the inspector skips re-rendering; selection-changed and external scene-changed (reload, drag-drop) still trigger a fresh render because focus has left the inspector. Canvas re-renders on scene-changed independently.

Save endpoint round-trip normalizes scene.json formatting: original title/scene.json was hand-formatted with collapsed {} objects on single lines, while JSON.stringify(body, null, 2) always expands every object. This is intentional per the spec ("stable 2-space pretty-print so diffs stay clean across editor and agent surfaces") — once both editor and agent save through the endpoint, future diffs will be clean. Restored the original title/scene.json after smoke-testing so the CP5 commit doesn't bundle the one-time normalization with the feature changes; first real save will normalize it.

Header bar lives outside .editor-shell as a sibling under <body>. Switched <body> to a 36px+1fr CSS grid and reduced .editor-shell height to calc(100vh - 36px). Keeps the existing four-panel grid intact and gives the toolbar a fixed height without competing with the canvas/inspector layout.

Verification limitation (same as CP1-CP4): no browser available so the visual/interactive outcome (drag CODECAINE onto canvas → layer added; type into inspector number field → canvas re-renders live; drag hierarchy row to reorder; click Save → button disables, scene.json round-trips) is not eyeballed. Verified all plumbing: vite build succeeds; dev server boots in ~90 ms; all editor modules transform with HTTP 200 (state.js, panels/inspector.js, panels/canvas-drop.js, panels/hierarchy.js, panels/asset-browser.js, panels/toolbar.js, loader.js); save endpoint returns 204 on valid PUT and writes correct JSON, 400 on invalid id (Bad_Id), 400 on invalid JSON body, 400 on non-object body ([]), 405 on GET. Move-into-self guard in moveLayer + descendant string-prefix check in hierarchy onDrop prevent the cycle case. User should run npm --prefix apps/scene-engine run dev and open /editor/?scene=title to confirm the authoring loop.

Plan asked for @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Orbitron') as a fallback. Instead copied apps/frontend/public/fonts/FolkPro_Family/ to apps/scene-engine/public/fonts/FolkPro_Family/ and inlined the four FolkPro @font-face rules + the --amber custom property at the top of stage.css. This keeps the title look pixel-identical to the legacy frontend without an external font CDN dependency, and still works after apps/frontend/ is deleted in task 6.3.9.

Plan task description listed sub-layer names like 'Chrome Depth/Extrusion Shadow', 'Interior/Red Fill', 'Chrome/Top' but those slash-paths do not exist in the actual CODECAINE.css-layers.svg — the SVG only has kebab-case data-layer attributes (chrome-extrusion-shadow-layer, fill-layer, red-enamel-gloss-layer, etc.). Preserved the working CP3 children that reference real data-layer ids and added in-text-fire interleaved between fill-layer and red-enamel-gloss for the chrome/red sandwich. Added top-level press-start (component) at center/75%, start-cue (audio, volume 0.6, autoplay), and crt (effect) layers per the plan; total 5 top-level layers.

Plan task 8 left asset bundling unspecified — with root='.' and publicDir='public', the apps/scene-engine/assets/ tree is served in dev (Vite serves project root as static) but is NOT copied to dist/ by default. Added a small inline `copyStaticAssetsPlugin` (apply: 'build') in vite.config.js that uses fs.cp to recursively copy `assets/` → `dist/assets/` and copies each discovered scene.json into `dist/scenes/<id>/scene.json` during closeBundle. Build now produces a self-contained deployable dist/: redirect index.html, per-scene HTML+JSON, editor HTML, all assets/{glyphs,media,effects,components,audio,registry.json}, and Vite-bundled JS/CSS chunks under dist/assets/. The benign INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT warning from CP3 is unchanged.

Repo has no root package.json — there is no workspaces array to update. The only non-historical reference to `apps/frontend` outside .spectre/ was the Makefile's FRONTEND_DIR variable + the help text. Retargeted FRONTEND_DIR to `apps/scene-engine` so `make dev` / `make build` / `make preview` continue to work after deletion. Updated the help-text path string to `apps/scene-engine/dist/`. Other hits remain in .spectre/sessions/** (historical session logs) and .claude/commands/prime/*.md (those reference an unrelated Spectre/Pi Next.js dashboard, not this repo's apps/frontend) — left untouched. apps/frontend/ removed via rm -rf.

Verification limitation (same as CP1–CP5): no browser available so the visual/audio outcome (bg video + chrome CODECAINE with in-text fire interleave + blinking PRESS START + CRT scanlines + start-cue beep on first user gesture) is not eyeballed. Verified plumbing: `npm run build` succeeds in ~50ms producing dist/index.html (redirect) + dist/scenes/title/{index.html,scene.json} + dist/editor/index.html + dist/assets/{glyphs,media,effects,components,audio,registry.json} + Vite-bundled JS/CSS chunks. ensureAllSceneHtml runs at vite-config load time and auto-generated scenes/title/index.html with `window.__SCENE_ID__ = 'title'` + module script. Component renderer dynamic-imports asset modules with a moduleCache + ensureStylesheet sidecar; audio renderer mirrors the pattern minus CSS + position. apps/frontend/ removed; Makefile retargeted at apps/scene-engine. User should run `npm --prefix apps/scene-engine run dev` and open / (→ /scenes/title/) to confirm the full vertical-slice fidelity, plus `npm --prefix apps/scene-engine run preview` to confirm the production build renders identically.
